item.title: #3592123: Canvas AI: removeMediaFields() drops arrays of media IDs for multi-value media props
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592123 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

When you ask the Canvas AI agent to place a component that has a multi-value image prop and name several media items, for example "Use media images 1 to 5", those media are now kept. Before, the list was dropped and the component showed its example images. A single media ID already worked.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

removeMediaFields() in ui/src/components/aiExtension/placementUtils.ts strips values a media-bound prop cannot store, so the component falls back to its example image. It previously kept only a single media ID (isMediaId()). The fix adds an exported isMediaIdList() helper and removeMediaFields() now also keeps a value when isMediaIdList(value) is true.

isMediaIdList() returns true only for a non-empty array where every item passes isMediaId(), so numbers and digit-only strings are accepted. Empty arrays and arrays mixing IDs with URLs or { src, alt } objects are still dropped. Tests in placementUtils.test.tsx cover these cases.

item.title: #3592176: Duplicating a page template silently does nothing: the GET representation is no longer a valid POST body
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592176 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The "Duplicate" action in the Templates panel (Page templates) now works. In Canvas 1.12.0 it appeared to do nothing, because the server rejected the request with a 422 and the UI hid the error. A copy of a disabled template now stays disabled, and any failure to duplicate is shown as an error card in the panel with a Dismiss button.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The GET representation of a page variant, since #3592106, includes the computed inputs_resolved and explicit null values for optional keys. buildDuplicateVariantPayload() in ui/src/services/pageVariants.ts spread each response item into the POST body, so POST /canvas/api/v0/config/page_variant failed validation. The fix is client-side only (the issue's Option A), so the server and the CLI, which reads inputs_resolved, are untouched. Each tree item is now rebuilt from storable keys: uuid, component_id, component_version, inputs, and parent_uuid, slot and label only when non-null. The status of the source is also carried over.

In ui/src/types/PageVariant.ts, a new PageVariantComponentTreeItemResponse type (nullable optional keys plus inputs_resolved) is used for PageVariant.component_tree. This way TypeScript rejects passing a read item where the write type PageVariantComponentTreeItem is expected. CreatePageVariantPayload gains an optional status. In PageVariants.tsx, handleDuplicate() now stores the rejection in duplicateError and renders an ErrorCard. The commit also adds a unit test and a Playwright test in pageVariants.spec.ts.

item.title: #3592122: Canvas AI: get_component_details and get_component_context omit item type and item limits of multi-value props
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592122 · 1 contributor · 26 comments

Summary

The Canvas AI get_component_details function, and get_component_context with catalog_only set to false, now describe multi-value props fully. Before, an array prop showed only type: array, so an AI agent could not tell what each value should be or how many values were allowed. The output now includes the item type and the minItems and maxItems limits when the component sets them. Defaults of formatted text arrays are now HTML strings instead of a list of null values.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In CanvasAiPageBuilderHelper, a new private getMultiValuePropMetadata() runs for props whose schema type is array. It adds items, normalized through propMetadataNormalizer with PropShape::normalizePropSchema() so format, contentMediaType and enum come through. It also copies minItems and maxItems when they are set. The method is used on both the SDC/default path and the JS component path.

Default values that are arrays are now mapped item by item, with MarkupInterface items cast to strings. This fixes the multi-value formatted text defaults.

For code (JS) components, the prop schema is no longer taken from the client-side jsonSchema plus a manual copy of meta:enum and x-translation-context. It is now built from getJavaScriptComponent()->toSdcDefinition()['props']['properties'] and passed through componentPluginManager->resolveJsonSchemaReferences(), which keeps meta:enum. The constructor type hint changed to Drupal\canvas\Plugin\ComponentPluginManager. Tests were added to GetComponentDetailsTest, along with a new formatted-text-list fixture component in the canvas_ai_test module.

item.title: #3592216: Workspaces PR 2: hard dependency on core Workspaces, Main workspace, install and test scaffolding
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592216 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

This is the first MR of the Workspaces series on the 1.x-workspaces feature branch (planned in #3592187). Canvas now requires core Workspaces. Installing Canvas, or updating a 1.x site, enables workspaces and creates an undeletable "Main Canvas workspace" (canvas_default). Auto-save still uses the 1.x key-value store at the end of this MR, so editors see no change in how drafts are saved. The MR also adds ADR 0022, the design for staging Canvas drafts in workspaces, where the whole workspace is the unit of publish and per-item publish goes away. That ADR is marked "Proposed" and describes behaviour that later MRs in the series implement.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Core workspaces module becomes a required dependency of Canvas (core floor unchanged at ^11.3).
  • Database update: canvas_update_11201() (partial) enables workspaces and creates the Main workspace; Page owner and metatag fields become revisionable, with the update for existing sites in a later MR.
  • Config change: A canvas_default workspace ("Main Canvas workspace") is created on install/update and cannot be deleted while Canvas is installed.
  • New API: New Drupal\canvas\AutoSave\Workspace\AutoSaveWorkspace class with ID and LABEL constants.

Technical details

The Main workspace ID and label live in the new AutoSaveWorkspace class (ID = 'canvas_default'). WorkspaceAutoSaveRevisionHooks blocks deleting it: workspace_access forbids the delete operation, and workspace_predelete throws a LogicException for programmatic deletes. Per the issue description, the install and update code is canvas_install(), _canvas_ensure_auto_save_workspace() and a partial canvas_update_11201(). I could not read those files in the diff I received, so I have not checked them.

WorkspaceAutoSaveHooks::entityTypeBuild() assigns core's IgnoredWorkspaceHandler as the workspace handler on config entity types provided by canvas or a canvas_* module. Without it, core refuses to save those entities while a workspace is active.

Page now marks the owner field revisionable, and the metatag field on pages is also revisionable. A pending revision only carries revisionable fields, so this stops draft changes from skipping the draft and landing on the live page. The issue says an update for existing sites is planned as canvas_update_11202() in a later MR. ViewModeDisplayController now type-hints FormController instead of HtmlEntityFormController, because Workspaces decorates controller.entity_form. ApiConfigControllers, ApiContentControllers and ApiTranslationControllers gain a nullable WorkspaceManagerInterface $workspaceManager constructor argument, autowired from workspaces.manager. Per the comment in the diff, it is NULL while a 1.x site has not yet run canvas_update_11201(). It is not read yet: each is marked with a @todo Workspaces PR 5 and PHPStan ignores.

ComponentSourceManager takes a new TypedConfigManagerInterface and returns early from component generation when canvas.component_source_settings.* has no config schema. This covers the case where Canvas and Workspaces install in one batch and Layout Builder's cache tag invalidator clears the block manager before Canvas's schema is available. The workspace_switcher block is added to the excluded list in BlockComponentDiscovery. EntityFieldPropSourceMatcher skips fields that are explicitly internal, such as Workspaces' workspace revision field, using TypedDataHelper::isExplicitlyInternal().

Tests and docs make up the rest. The tests install workspaces, add the workspace cache context to expected responses, and add a WorkspacesDependencyUpdateTest update-path test. The docs are ADR 0022, docs/diagrams/workspace-autosave.md and a docs/personalization.md update. A @todo Workspaces PR convention is documented in the branch's PR-landing skill file.

Upgrade

Sites on Canvas 1.x updating to this branch should run database updates: per the issue, canvas_update_11201() enables workspaces and creates the canvas_default workspace. Core Workspaces is a core module, so there is no composer change, and the core floor stays ^11.3. Tests that install Canvas now also need workspaces and its schemas, a canvas_default workspace, and the workspace cache context in expected cache contexts. Controllers that read through controller.entity_form should type-hint Drupal\Core\Controller\FormController rather than HtmlEntityFormController.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 19, 2026

item.title: #3591889: Canvas Editor: Component collapses and becomes un-clickable on the canvas when all media props are removed
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591889 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the Canvas editor, if you removed every image from a component's media props through the Settings panel, the component rendered as blank on the canvas. It then had no size, so you could not click it to select it or reopen its settings. The issue is marked fixed. Its stated expected behavior is that the component returns to its default empty state, with placeholders or blank image boxes as when first added, and stays clickable.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

No fix diff or comments were available for this issue, and I did not find the fix in the repository history I checked. I could not verify how it was fixed. The report describes the bug as the component rendering nothing once its last media prop is cleared, instead of its default empty state. A related earlier fix, #3591857, changed DrupalMediaListContainer.tsx so that removing one media item no longer deleted the stored values of other media-backed props on the same component.

item.title: #3592120: Canvas AI: Give the Canvas Agent editor-facing knowledge about Drupal Canvas
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592120 · 1 contributor · 20 comments

Summary

The Drupal Canvas Agent in the canvas_dev_ai module used to know only which Tool to select for a task and where the documentation lives. It could not answer questions like "How do I translate a page?" or "What is a page template?". Its prompt now includes editor-facing facts about the Canvas interface: pages, building a page, patterns, saving and publishing, page and content templates, translations, code components, and missing theme components. It is told to answer from those facts using the exact interface labels. When a question is not covered, it says so and points to https://project.pages.drupalcode.org/canvas/ instead of inventing an answer.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: modules/canvas_dev_ai/config/install/ai_agents.ai_agent.canvas_agent.yml has a rewritten system_prompt with editor-facing facts about Canvas.

Technical details

The change is confined to the system_prompt in modules/canvas_dev_ai/config/install/ai_agents.ai_agent.canvas_agent.yml. The prompt is restructured around two cases. Case A is a question, the default, answered only from a "Facts" section at the end of the prompt. Case B is a request to do the work, which the agent redirects to a Tool using the [canvas_dev_ai:available_tools] placeholder, with the existing Tool selection behaviour kept. Guardrails say never to add steps, labels, permissions, features or URLs that are not in the facts, to give only URLs that appear in the prompt, and to treat other Drupal or Canvas knowledge as unknown. Personalization, headless frontends, notifications and conflict resolution are explicitly declared out of scope, so the agent says so and gives the docs link. The facts were drafted by scanning the docs/ folder and the UI code with Claude, per the issue body, and then verified against the UI.

Upgrade

The prompt lives in config/install, so it applies on fresh installs of canvas_dev_ai. The issue says no update hook is added, so existing sites keep their stored canvas_agent config until it is reimported or re-saved.

Contribution

item.title: #3592021: Canvas AI: Unify error handling in `canvas_component_agent`'s tools
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592021 · 1 contributor · 50 comments

Summary

The Canvas AI tools used by canvas_component_agent now report every validation problem at once instead of stopping at the first one, so the model can fix everything in a single retry. The tools also refuse to run for users without the Canvas AI permission. The error text sent back to the model changes from YAML error: output to a markdown list.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Permission change: GetJsComponent, GetPropsType, CreateComponent and EditComponentJs now throw unless the current user has CanvasAiPermissions::USE_CANVAS_AI.

Technical details

This applies the pattern from #3591958 (already used by place_components and edit_components) to the JS component tools. CreateComponent and EditComponentJs now start with the access check, which throws unchanged. Every other check adds to an $errors array keyed by item label (Component, Slots, Slot <index>), and the array is reported through AiResponseValidator::formatErrors(). That output starts with "Nothing was applied. Fix every error listed below and call the tool again." and has one ## section per item with bullet errors. The message is logged as a warning and set as the tool output, so a failing call applies nothing.

In AiGeneratedJsComponentPropsAndSlotsTrait, transformSlotsMetadata() now takes an array &$errors by-reference parameter instead of throwing. It collects an error for each bad slot and leaves invalid slots out of the returned slots, so the remaining structure is still validated in the same pass. In EditComponentJs the structure validation runs only when the component was found. The @apply CSS check and the "component already exists" check in CreateComponent now accumulate rather than returning early. Constraint violations from JavaScriptComponent::createFromClientSide() are added under Component using the ConstraintViolationException message.

Unexpected exceptions are still caught and logged. Their output is now plain text, Failed to create the component: ... or Failed to update the component: .... It was previously Yaml::dump(['error' => 'Failed to process Javascript component data: ...']). GetJsComponent and GetPropsType gain the same USE_CANVAS_AI permission check. GetPropsType gets a create() method to inject AccountProxyInterface. Kernel tests for the four tools were updated, and a new GetPropsTypeTest was added.

Upgrade

Any code that parses the YAML error: output of CreateComponent or EditComponentJs must handle the new plain-text and markdown messages. The transformSlotsMetadata() trait method now takes a second argument, array &$errors, instead of throwing.

item.title: #3592226: Workspaces PR 3: workspace-scoped auto-save (the core change)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592226 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, every Canvas draft is now staged in the active core Workspace, or in the Main workspace when none is active, instead of in the 1.x key-value auto-save store. This is PR 3 of a planned series. It covers the storage and manager layers. The controllers (PR 5) and per-item publish replacement (PR 7a) land separately. Per the issue, ApiAutoSaveControllerTest fails after this PR until PR 7a, and the 1.x post() publish is unsafe inside a workspace until then. This is an intermediate step on a feature branch. Its description is a plan, and the merge request was never linked to it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: Per-workspace key-value collections canvas.auto_save.{workspace} and canvas.auto_save_meta.{workspace} replace the single 1.x canvas.auto_save collection.
  • API change: AutoSaveManager auto-save keys become workspace-prefixed ({workspace}:{type}:{id}[:{langcode}]), and Canvas content drafts are now staged in the active workspace instead of the 1.x key-value store.
  • New API: New AutoSaveFallbackStore and WorkspaceAutoSave services under src/AutoSave/Workspace/; AutoSaveManager delegates to them.

Technical details

The design is ADR 0022, which landed in PR 2. Content entity drafts become the entity's single tracked pending revision in the active workspace, and the previous one is deleted. Config entity drafts, and content drafts the storage layer rejects (for example an invalid component tree that throws in presave), go to a per-workspace fallback store, AutoSaveFallbackStore. That store uses the collections canvas.auto_save.{ws} for draft rows and canvas.auto_save_meta.{ws} for client instance, draft path and attribution. It caps workspace IDs at 100 characters and offers deleteWorkspace() and workspaceIds(). Exactly one store holds a target's current draft: a fallback row shadows the primary store until the next successful primary persist. Staging never validates. ClientDataToEntityConverter converts and validates inside the staging workspace so core's one-workspace-per-entity lock passes. Writes are idempotent, and dirty state is computed at read time by hashing staged data against Live.

WorkspaceAutoSave (about 1,300 lines per the issue) holds the persist, read, discard and delete logic. AutoSaveManager delegates to it, adds workspace-prefixed keys, and gains executeInStagingWorkspace(), getEntityForLayoutEditing(), deleteTranslation() and a forcePreserve option. onCanvasConfigEntitySave() checks isPublishTimeStaging(). A cross-workspace lock raises WorkspaceEntityLockedException, which ApiExceptionSubscriber maps to a 409 with a new ErrorCodesEnum code (8). The 1.x hash-based conflict detection is kept: the base hash of a content draft is recorded in the metadata collection, and fallback rows keep original_hash. It is compared against WorkspaceAutoSave::loadUnchangedBase(). AutoSaveWorkspacePublishSubscriber::validateItem() adds the AutoSaveEntityConflictConstraint violation for a Page draft with an unresolved conflict. ContentTemplate is now created enabled, and the translation synchronizer skips staged non-default translations. AutoSaveManager::groupContentEntityAutoSaves() and autoSavePublish() stay until PR 7a. The planned tests include WorkspaceAutoSaveStagingTest.

The MR for this PR was not attached, and the issue has no comments. I read the issue text and the reference branch MR 1845, whose diff was partial and omitted WorkspaceAutoSave.php and AutoSaveManager.php. I did not read the final merged code of this PR.

Upgrade

Existing 1.x key-value drafts are not migrated by this PR. The issue says canvas_post_update_0026 is unchanged. The reference branch has a LegacyAutoSaveMigrator that moves them into the Main workspace, but I did not confirm it lands here. Code that reads auto-save keys must handle the new {workspace}:{type}:{id}[:{langcode}] form.

Contribution

item.title: #3592109: CLI pull/push loses entity references and options in component link props
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592109 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Pulling and pushing pages or page templates with the Canvas CLI no longer degrades component link props. A link stored as entity:node/7 with a target="_blank" option used to come back as internal:/node/7 with empty options, even when nobody edited it. Unchanged links now keep their original URI and options. If you edit the URL, the link is rebuilt as before, with empty options.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Pages and page templates pull through resolvedComponentTreeToAuthoredElementMap(), which writes link props as plain resolved URL strings. The old extractMediaProvenance() is now extractPropProvenance() in packages/cli/src/utils/authored-elements.ts. Besides media references, it records { uri, options, resolved_url } in the element's _provenance for any link prop (stored input with a string uri and options, resolved to a string).

On push, linkTransformer.serialize() in packages/cli/src/utils/prop-transforms.ts gets the provenance. If provenance.resolved_url equals the authored string, it returns the original { uri, options }. Otherwise it uses the existing normalization, such as the internal: prefix, with empty options. resolved_url is local metadata and is never sent to Drupal. Content templates were not affected, because their pull path already keeps the raw link object. The change ships as a patch changeset for @drupal-canvas/cli.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 21, 2026

item.title: #3592225: Workspaces PR 3: workspace-scoped auto-save (the core change)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592225 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

This is the core change of the Canvas Workspaces integration, developed on the 1.x-workspaces branch. Every Canvas draft is now staged in the active workspace instead of the 1.x key-value auto-save store. Content entity drafts are kept as workspace revisions. Config entities that can't be staged that way are kept in per-workspace fallback storage. Drafts in different workspaces are separate. An entity that another workspace has claimed is locked, and the API reports this as a 409 conflict. This issue is a planning and tracking record. Its body describes the intended scope and has no linked merge request or comments, so the wording below follows the plan, not merged code.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Builds on PR 2 (#3592216), which made Workspaces a hard dependency of Canvas on the 1.x-workspaces branch.
  • New API: New WorkspaceAutoSave and AutoSaveFallbackStore classes under src/AutoSave/Workspace/, and a new WorkspaceEntityLockedException.

Technical details

The issue body says the change is split from the controllers (PR 5) by call direction: everything below the controllers lands here. I could not check the merged code. The 1.x-workspaces branch I cloned didn't contain these classes yet, and the issue has no linked merge request.

Per the plan, the main pieces are:

  • AutoSaveFallbackStore uses per-workspace collections named canvas.auto_save.{ws} and canvas.auto_save_meta.{ws}. It has a workspace ID length guard, deleteWorkspace() and workspaceIds().
  • WorkspaceAutoSave is the engine. It covers persisting staged entities, claiming an entity for a workspace, keeping only the latest revision, and retaining a fallback draft when the storage throws. It also covers loading and listing drafts, discard and delete, staging fallback drafts, and clearing workspace stores.
  • AutoSaveManager delegates to the engine, uses workspace-prefixed keys, and adds executeInStagingWorkspace(), getEntityForLayoutEditing(), deleteTranslation() and a forcePreserve option. onCanvasConfigEntitySave() also gets an isPublishTimeStaging() check.
  • Supporting changes: WorkspaceEntityLockedException, a new code 8 in ErrorCodesEnum, and the lock-to-409 mapping in ApiExceptionSubscriber.
  • ClientDataToEntityConverter validates inside the staging workspace and raises changed to the request time.
  • The symmetrical translation synchronizer skips staged non-default translations.
  • ContentTemplate is created enabled.
  • Conflict detection is kept from the 1.x branch. The base hash is stored in the workspace meta collection (or as original_hash on a fallback row) and compared against loadUnchangedBase().

The plan lists known gaps after this PR: ApiAutoSaveControllerTest fails until PR 7a replaces per-item publish, the 1.x post() is unsafe inside a workspace, and the PR 5 controllers still read Live content.

item.title: #3592211: Workspaces PR 1: retire the 1.x external-edit conflict detection
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592211 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas removes the experimental 1.x conflict detection that was enabled by the canvas_dev_cd module. That flow detected when an entity was saved outside Canvas after an auto-save, then blocked publishing and offered a /conflict resolution page. It is replaced by core's Workspaces EntityWorkspaceConflict lock, planned in a later step of the Workspaces work. This step targets the 1.x-workspaces branch. Sites that never installed canvas_dev_cd should see no change. The pending-changes endpoint now always returns 200 for conflict purposes, and validation errors are always 422.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Removed AutoSaveManager conflict methods and the with_conflicts argument of getAllAutoSaveList(), removed ErrorCodesEnum codes 4, 5 and 6, dropped resolved_conflict_id from the auto-save PATCH, and API errors are always 422, never 409.
  • Deprecation: The canvas_dev_cd module is marked hidden and obsolete, and its conflict detection and resolution flow is removed.

Technical details

This is the first step of the Workspaces plan (work item 3592187). It removes the hash-based flow, where an auto-save stored original_hash and a mismatch triggered a conflict. The issue body, not a verified diff, is the source for the details below.

Back end: the canvas_dev_cd module is hidden and marked obsolete. ConflictResolutionOutcomeEnum and AutoSaveEntityConflictConstraint are deleted. Codes 4, 5 and 6 are removed from ErrorCodesEnum. ApiControllerBase always returns 422 and never 409. The auto-save PATCH controller drops resolved_conflict_id and takes status only. ApiExceptionSubscriber loses its conflict-constraint branch. AutoSaveManager loses AUTO_SAVE_CONFLICT_KEY, AUTO_SAVE_STORED_ENTITY_HASH_KEY, getUnresolvedConflict(), getConflictId(), getUnresolvedConflictForEntity(), resolveConflict(), setStoredEntityHash() and the with_conflicts argument of getAllAutoSaveList(). The callers in ConfigAuditBase, Inventory and PageVariant are updated. ApiAutoSaveController drops autoSaveListHasConflicts(), the 409 branch of get() and getConflictAwareContentEntityViolations(). canvas_post_update_0026 now writes the literal 'original_hash' key because the constant is gone. The devConflictDetectionMode setting is dropped from DrupalSettings.ts and CanvasController.

UI: the ui/src/features/conflict/* code, conflict notifications, ConflictBanner, the /conflict route and conflict state in the change list components are removed. isReviewUxEnabled() in ui/src/features/review/reviewChanges.ts is now gated on devMode instead of canvas_dev_cd, so the side-by-side review page still works for developers. The related tests are removed, including testPatchConflictResolution and the Playwright conflictResolution.spec.ts. The issue gives the size as about 30 lines added and 3,900 removed.

Upgrade

Code that used canvas_dev_cd, a 409 response from GET /auto-saves/pending, error codes 4, 5 or 6, or resolved_conflict_id in the auto-save PATCH must stop depending on them. Code calling AutoSaveManager::getAllAutoSaveList() should drop the with_conflicts argument.

item.title: #3592085: Canvas AI: Let the user stop a running chat turn
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592085 · 1 contributor · 63 comments

Summary

In the Canvas AI dev chat (AiWizardDev), the user can now stop the agent while it is working. A stop button shows only during a running turn. Pressing it drops the in-flight request, stops applying further placements or edits, clears the loader, and unlocks the input and Tools selector. The chat adds the assistant message "You interrupted the agent. What would you like to change?" and the progress row shows a neutral stopped icon, not the completed check. Work already applied to the page stays, and the user can undo it from the editor. The next message starts a fresh turn and does not resume the stopped one. The server is not interrupted: PHP already running finishes its current step. The original non-dev AiWizard.tsx is untouched.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: CanvasAiTempStore::getStoredConversationState() now requires a $request_id argument. setStoredConversationState() now takes $request_id as its second argument and an optional $resumed_request_id as its last. The dev AI endpoint reads a new last_successful_request_id prompt key.
  • New API: New last_successful_request_id field in the dev AI request payload, naming the checkpoint the next turn resumes.

Technical details

The fix is in AiWizardDev.tsx and CanvasDevAiBuilder, in canvas_dev_ai. The client keeps a per-turn stopped flag that the hop loop and the placement and edit batches check (isStopped()), and it aborts the fetch. This is needed because aborting alone only rejects the current request.

A stopped turn can still finish on the server and write its agent state. If the next turn resumed that state, it could send an unrun tool call back to the model. To prevent this, the client now sends last_successful_request_id with every hop. This is the last turn that was fully applied and not stopped. CanvasDevAiBuilder::prepareAgent() resumes only the checkpoint stored under that request ID, and otherwise seeds the agent from the client transcript. A stopped turn is never named, so it is never resumed.

CanvasAiTempStore conversation state is now a map keyed by request ID. It holds at most two entries: the checkpoint the current turn resumed from, and the one it wrote. Older entries, including those from stopped turns, are dropped on the next write. When keep_tool_calls_in_history is off, or the turn fails or is not solvable, all checkpoints are deleted. placementUtils.ts was also changed so placements can be cut short when a stop lands.

Upgrade

Callers of the CanvasAiTempStore conversation methods must now pass request IDs:

$store->getStoredConversationState($conversation_id, $request_id);
$store->setStoredConversationState($conversation_id, $request_id, $agent_id, $state, $resumed_request_id);

Clients of the dev AI endpoint should send last_successful_request_id in the prompt payload. Without it the turn is seeded from the transcript.

item.title: #3592132: Allow modules to add operations to the Canvas content list
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3592132 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Modules can now add their own operations (for example "Translate") to each page in the Canvas pages panel and the page navigation menu. Previously the operations were a fixed set and contrib had no way to extend them. Operations only appear for users who have access to the operation's URL.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Content API entities gain an optional linkLabels property (link relation type to label), documented in openapi.yml; responses without module operations are unchanged.
  • New API: New hook_canvas_content_operation(EntityInterface $entity): array, the Canvas counterpart of hook_entity_operation().

Technical details

A module implements hook_canvas_content_operation(EntityInterface $entity) and returns an array keyed by a unique, module-prefixed name. Each item has title, url (a Url object) and an optional weight (default 0), the same shape as hook_entity_operation(). The key becomes the link relation type.

ApiContentControllers::getEntityOperations() now invokes the hook through the injected ModuleHandlerInterface (a new constructor argument). It checks access() on each Url for the current user. Accessible operations are added to the content entity's links as CanvasResourceLink items whose target attributes carry label and weight. Inaccessible ones only contribute cacheability, and the languages:language_interface cache context is added because labels are translatable.

Because the link collection is sorted by key, the response builder derives an ordered linkLabels map (relation type to label, sorted by weight) and emits it only when non-empty. On the frontend, the PageList.tsx and Navigation.tsx menus render these links between Canvas's own operations and "Delete page", using a new helper in ui/src/utils/contentOperations.ts and the linkLabels field in ui/src/types/Content.ts. Tests are a kernel test in ApiContentControllersListTest using a test hook in canvas_test_page, and a unit test for the UI helper.

Upgrade

A module that wants to add an operation implements the new hook (example from canvas.api.php):

function hook_canvas_content_operation(EntityInterface $entity): array {
  return [
    'my_module_translate' => [
      'title' => new TranslatableMarkup('Translate'),
      'url' => Url::fromUri('base:my-translation-ui/' . $entity->id()),
      'weight' => 50,
    ],
  ];
}

item.title: #3591748: Hydrate components with diamond dependencies
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591748 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

A code component that imports another code component and also directly imports one of that component's own dependencies no longer fails to hydrate. Previously, with Pricing importing Card and Button, and Card also importing Button, the browser threw Failed to resolve module specifier "@/components/demo_button" and the card did not render. The generated import map now includes a scope for every intermediate component, so such component trees render.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The bug was in the private JsComponent::getScopedDependencies(), which builds the per-component scopes entries of the import map. Its $seen array behaved as a global visited set shared across sibling branches. Because dependencies are sorted, the shared leaf (demo_button) was visited before the intermediate (demo_card). By the time the code recursed into Card, Button was already in $seen, so the loop skipped it and Card's own @/components/demo_button scope entry was never written. The browser then had no scope to resolve the import inside Card's module.

The fix makes $seen the current recursion path (ancestors only). $seen[] = $component->id() is added at the start of each call, and the @/components/{name} entry for the component's scope is now written before the cycle check. A dependency that is an ancestor on the current path still continues to avoid infinite recursion, but only after its scope entry has been recorded. The existing step that merges a dependency's scope into its parent's scope is unchanged.

getDependencyLibraries() has the same $seen shape but was not changed in the merged commit. The issue notes global deduplication is desirable for libraries, but its remaining-task checkbox to confirm it cannot drop a needed library in a diamond was left unchecked. The issue also describes a kernel test, JsComponentTest::testImportMapsWithDiamondDependency().

item.title: #3591848: ∅ is added for empty fields, forcing translation and rendering on the page
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591848 · 1 contributor · 8 comments

Summary

When translating Canvas Pages with TMGMT, empty component inputs no longer show a literal ∅ in the review form or force the translator to fill them in. An input that is empty in the source now reads "This field is empty in the source language." An optional input can be left blank in the translation and is saved as empty. A required input still gives TMGMT's "The field is empty." error. If a translator plugin returns an exact ∅, it is discarded and the value from the default translation is kept. This fixes content translation only. Config translation jobs (ContentTemplate, PageRegion) still show, force and store ∅. Falling back to the source value at render time is not part of this change.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ComponentInputsTranslatablesExtractor::EMPTY_SENTINEL (∅) is still the extracted #text for empty optional inputs, because TMGMT's Data::flatten() strips empty strings. It is now an internal marker only. TmgmtHooks implements hook_tmgmt_data_item_text_output_alter to blank it in both review columns, but only for content job items whose entity has a Canvas field. It also implements hook_form_tmgmt_job_item_edit_form_alter and hook_form_tmgmt_local_task_item_edit_form_alter. These replace the missing source textarea with a message. They also add validate callbacks that temporarily set the sentinel on empty translations of optional props, so TMGMT's "The field is empty." check passes, and restore the empty value afterwards. Required props, checked via prop_field_definitions[...]['required'] of the component version the tree item uses, are not masked and keep the error. The "Validate" and "Save as completed" buttons are handled the same way. The local task form (tmgmt_local) gets a parallel set of mask and unmask callbacks.

In ComponentTreeFieldProcessor, writeNestedTranslationsToInputs() returns NULL for a translation that is exactly the sentinel. An empty string is kept as a valid, explicitly empty translation. If every translatable leaf of a composite input (such as text_format) is NULL, the whole composite becomes NULL. setTranslations() then refills NULL values at any depth from the default translation via refillDiscardedFromDefault() and defaultTranslationInputs(). Values that stay NULL are dropped. Only an exact match is discarded, so a translation that merely contains ∅ is stored as written.

ComponentInputsTranslatablesExtractor also gets getUnresolvedSchemaDefinition(). It reads the config schema before type resolution, because core rewrites definitions in place and removes type. Without it, text_format inputs could lose their #format. A @todo points to work item 3592014 for extending the sentinel handling to config job items.

item.title: #3591930: Apply brand kit colour changes optimistically
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3591930 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Editing or adding a brand kit colour in the Canvas editor now updates the swatch right away instead of waiting for the server. The form closes on save, and the editor reverts the change if the server rejects it. The colour change also reaches the page preview while the editor stays open, which didn't happen before. This also fixes colour edits not showing when a brand kit auto-save draft existed, for example after a font edit.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The changes are all in the ui/ React app. In ui/src/services/brandKit.ts, updateColor and createColor now patch the getBrandKit cache entry in onQueryStarted through a patchColors() helper, and call patchResult.undo() if the request fails. Each patch mutates a single colour in place, so undoing it cannot revert an edit to a different colour. updateColor also records a Symbol token per colour id in latestColorWrites. It rolls back only if its token is still the newest for that id, so a slow failing request cannot overwrite a later edit. createColor inserts a temporary row with a pending-<uuid> id and swaps in the server's row when the response arrives. It does not mint the final UUID on the client, which the issue body proposed. The invalidated tag changed from the literal 'global' to BRAND_KIT_ID.

useBrandKitColors now reads colours only from the canonical getBrandKit entry and no longer prefers the auto-save draft. The hook uses data instead of currentData, so optimistic patches stay visible during the refetch triggered by invalidation. The local colors state and setColors are removed. BrandKit.colors becomes optional in the type.

ColorFormPopover dispatches the mutation, then closes the popover. On failure it reopens through reopenOnFailure(), keeping the entered values and the error. For the preview, Viewport builds CSS custom properties from the live brand kit with buildColorStyles. It passes them to IframeSwapper as a new required headStyles prop. IframeSwapper injects them as a <style id="canvas-preview-head-styles"> block at the end of <head>. It updates already-loaded iframes in place and re-applies the block when a new preview iframe finishes loading.

item.title: #3592052: Site template installation fails with Canvas 1.11
item.description:

  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed

Summary

Installing a Drupal CMS site template (drush si recipes/drupal_cms_starter) failed with Canvas 1.11.0, with the error "You have requested a synthetic service ("kernel"). The DIC does not know how to construct this service." The reporter found that downgrading to Canvas 1.10.1 made the install work again. The issue is marked fixed. A related fix to the site template install path is in Canvas 1.12.0, but the issue thread does not confirm that it is the fix for this report.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The issue has no comments and no linked merge request, so the cause and fix are not stated there. I inferred a likely fix from the repository. Commit 64c59639 (#3591996, first tagged in v1.12.0) changes RecipeSubscriber so that site template page variant migration runs in a new migrateSiteTemplate() handler. That handler is registered on RecipeAppliedEvent at priority PHP_INT_MIN, so it runs after all other applied subscribers. Its docblock says installing the page template component module rebuilds the container, and that running last stops later subscribers from using the invalidated container. That matches the symptom, since a rebuilt container can fail on the synthetic kernel service. No commit references #3592052 directly, so treat the link as likely, not confirmed.

Upgrade

If site template installs fail on Canvas 1.11.0, either update to Canvas 1.12.0 or later, or pin the version the reporter confirmed works: composer require drupal/canvas:1.10.1.
